text: In BB84, if an eavesdropper performs the intercept-resend attack — measuring every photon in a randomly guessed basis and resending her result — what quantum bit error rate (QBER) does she introduce?
choices: 0%, because resending an identical photon leaves no trace
50%, since half the photons are lost
explanation: When Eve guesses the wrong basis (probability 1/2) and Bob's basis then happens to match Alice's, his outcome is random, giving (1/2)(1/2) = 25% QBER — a blazing alarm against the ~1-3% of a clean system. Choice 1 is the security abort threshold (11%), not the attack's induced error; choice 0 ignores basis mismatch; choice 3 confuses error rate with photon loss.
